Figure 1:Completed scene meshes generated byAnchorComplete.From a sparse, noisy point cloud,AnchorCompleterecovers a complete, metric-scale mesh,
shown with the house’s floors pulled apart and insets that pair the input with our mesh.
One model covers all three scales and fills in what the input never observed.

Figure 2:Overview ofAnchorComplete.From a partial, colored point cloud, Stage 1 generates a metric-scale octree coarse to fine, one window at a time, and Stage 2 generates shape latents on the finest level, which are decoded, merged and meshed once. Each window is conditioned on its parent occupancy and visible points through the local path (warm start) and on its points through anchor tokens read by cross-attention (global path).

Figure 3:Coarse-to-fine levels.The same model stopped at levels 0, 1 and 2 on a room corner of a real-world scene, with the mean F-scores ofTable2(b) on the right. Only level 2 separates the ladder rungs and the legs of the chair.

Figure 4:Qualitative reconstruction results on Replica(Straub et al., 2019)and SCRREAM(Jung et al., 2024).Given the same DA3 point cloud as input, our method achieves better scene completion performance.

Figure 5:Real-world scenes.Two real-world rooms from eight views, top-down with an inside view inset (same camera in every column); NKSR(Huang et al., 2023), SG-NN(Dai et al., 2020), Seen2Scene(Meng et al., 2026)andAnchorCompletetake the same input. The baselines leave surfaces holed where coverage thins, while ours closes them.

Figure 7:Sparse-view conditional scene completion.The DA3 input (top) loses coverage as views are removed, while our completion (bottom) stays closed across the range. Bottom row:AnchorCompleteat level 0,N=4N{=}4to1414views; Replica provides 10 input frames per scene, soN=12N{=}12and1414add held-out frames of the same sequence.

Figure 9:Additional qualitative results on Replica(Straub et al., 2019)atN=4N{=}4.Top-down views of the meshes each method reconstructs from the same partial DA3 point cloud, with the ground truth in the last column.

Figure 10:Additional qualitative results on SCRREAM(Jung et al., 2024)atN=4N{=}4.Top-down views of the meshes each method reconstructs from the same partial DA3 point cloud, with the ground truth in the last column.

Figure 11:Generation diversity.The input point cloud and five samples drawn from it with different seeds, rendered at level 0 with a model
trained on InternScenes and SAGE. The observed structure is kept in every sample, and the samples differ only in
the regions the input does not cover.

Figure 12:Failure cases under degraded imagery.Real captures with simulated low light (top) and motion blur/noise (bottom). The degraded inputs cause DA3 to miss large scene regions, and our model completes around these gaps rather than recovering them.
